The statement’s near-term outlook is negative—COVID-19 will depress activity and raise downside risks—but the policy response materially mitigates those risks. Theory and evidence suggest the announced tools are well targeted: at the zero lower bound, commitment and forward guidance can stimulate via expectations (Eggertsson and Woodford), while large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS reduce term and mortgage premia through portfolio-balance effects (event studies such as Gagnon et al.; Krishnamurthy and Vissing-Jorgensen). The broad liquidity backstops (discount window, repo operations, and dollar swap lines) directly counter the financial accelerator (Bernanke, Gertler, and Gilchrist), helping to stabilize credit spreads and the flow of funds. With market-based inflation compensation down but longer-term expectations little changed, a highly accommodative stance aligns with policy-rule insights (Rudebusch and Svensson) to support a return toward the 2 percent objective. Net assessment: still negative because of the shock, but less so given the strength and design of the response.
